root_cause: Dependant._unwrapped_call used only inspect.unwrap(self.call), which follows __wrapped__ but not functools.partial. The predicates is_coroutine_callable / is_gen_callable / is_async_gen_callable then inspect the partial object itself. inspect.isroutine(partial) is False and partial.__call__ is not a coroutine function, so partial(async_fn) was treated as sync and its un-awaited coroutine became the dependency value. For partial(callable_instance) the dunder lookup found partial.__call__ instead of the instance's __call__, so generator/async callable classes were misclassified. inspect.isgeneratorfunction/isasyncgenfunction already see through partials of plain functions, which is why those cases already worked.
best_solution: In fastapi/dependencies/models.py, Dependant._unwrapped_call: after unwrapped = inspect.unwrap(self.call), add `if isinstance(unwrapped, partial): unwrapped = unwrapped.func` (import partial from functools). Every sync/async/generator predicate reads _unwrapped_call, so this one normalization point fixes all of them: they now inspect the underlying function, bound method or callable instance, and the existing dunder-__call__ fallback works on the real instance. Signature and parameter extraction already handled partials, because inspect.signature drops the bound args. You can get to this from the statement alone: 'plain functions work, async and callable classes don't' points at sync/async classification rather than signature parsing, and grepping for iscoroutinefunction/isgeneratorfunction in fastapi/dependencies lands on these cached properties.
acceptable_alternatives: Loop `while isinstance(call, functools.partial): call = call.func` before or after inspect.unwrap (handles nested partials; this is what v4 did). A duck-typed hasattr(call, 'func') loop also passed (v8) but is fragile. Patching only get_typed_signature/get_typed_return_annotation in utils.py is NOT enough.
hidden_test_demands: New tests/test_dependency_partial.py::test_dependency_types_with_partial, parametrized over 12 routes. Each GET must return 200 with a JSON body equal to the string bound via partial. It covers Depends(partial(X, value)) where X is a sync function, async function, sync generator, async generator, callable instance (sync, sync-gen, async, async-gen __call__), and bound methods (sync, async, sync-gen, async-gen). No new API names. Behavior only.
locating_signals: The statement says 'dependables', 'functools.partial()', and 'partial of async and callable classes didn't work consistently'. It does not name the gold function (_unwrapped_call) or the file. The words 'async' and 'callable classes' point at the sync/async/generator classification on Dependant (is_coroutine_callable, is_gen_callable, is_async_gen_callable), all of which read _unwrapped_call. Grepping for inspect.unwrap or iscoroutinefunction under fastapi/dependencies finds it immediately. Existing tests/test_dependency_class.py (mentioned in the statement) shows the combination matrix to replicate.
our_outcome_summary: Kaggle env: v4 PASS, v8 PASS, v6 FAIL, v7 FAIL. v4 (339s, 50 calls) unwrapped nested partials with a while-isinstance loop before inspect.unwrap in _unwrapped_call, which is equivalent to gold. v8 (69s, 34 calls) looped on hasattr(current, 'func') plus inspect.unwrap in _unwrapped_call. It passes but would wrongly unwrap any object that has a .func attribute. v6 (327s, 24 calls) produced an empty patch. v7 (94s, 53 calls) edited the wrong place: it unwrapped partials only in get_typed_signature/get_typed_return_annotation in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, which only affects the globalns used for annotation resolution, and left Dependant._unwrapped_call untouched. 5 of 12 tests failed with ResponseValidationError (the partial async function, callable-gen, async callable, async callable-gen and async method cases), because a coroutine or generator object was returned as the value. The 7 cases that inspect already handled passed.
generalizable_lesson: When a wrapper (functools.partial, a decorator, a callable instance) breaks behavior, first work out which predicate makes the wrong decision (here: sync vs async vs generator dispatch) and fix the single normalization helper that feeds all such predicates. Do not fix whatever helper you happened to grep first (signature/annotation parsing). Before editing, write a 10-line repro that covers the full combination matrix the statement implies (sync/async x function/generator x function/instance/method). Run it before and after the fix, and do not stop while any cell still fails. Also: an empty patch is always a loss, so when time runs short, submit the smallest plausible fix at the central helper.
